title: Signed completed scalar shift coordinates and representative normalization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in one coefficient universe, a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-embedding $\iota:E\to L$, and a scheme $Y$ in an independent universe. Interpret the coefficient inclusion through $\iota$. Put $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$ for $F=E,L$, and use the completed coefficient module categories and quotient scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For $n\in\mathbf N$ (quotient exponent $n+1$), write
$$B_n(P)=\operatorname{Res}^L_{n+1}\bigl(P\otimes_{R_E}(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1})_Y\bigr),\qquad X_P=\prod_n B_n(P).$$
Use the actual quotient transitions $t_n:B_{n+1}(P)\to B_n(P)$, and define $h_P=1-s_P$ by $\mathrm{pr}_n h_P=\mathrm{pr}_n-t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]; this is the strict transition endomorphism of the coefficient-extension tower specified in [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The strict Roos cochain functor is $C(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(h_P)[-1]$, with its mapping-cocone convention as in [def-weil-signed-mapping-cocone-functor]. Let $Q$ be complex localization and use integer cochain shifts $P[m]^j=P^{j+m}$, $d_{P[m]}^j=(-1)^m d_P^{j+m}$, with the standard localization comparison $\eta_{P,m}:Q(P[m])\simeq(QP)[m]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A good complex means a K-flat complex with flat terms [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]. Use the derived scalar functor $T$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] and retain its natural representative comparison $d_P:T(QP)\simeq QC(P)$ on good complexes [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined].

A coherent integer shift structure on a functor $F$ means natural isomorphisms $e_{F,m,P}:F(P[m])\simeq F(P)[m]$, equal to the canonical identity comparison for $m=0$ and satisfying the addition law: under the standard associativity identifications, $e_{F,a+b,P}=e_{F,a,P}[b]\circ e_{F,b,P[a]}$. This specifies the meaning of the structures below, without asserting their existence.

Define $\operatorname{completedScalarShiftLevelIso}_{P,m,n}:B_n(P[m])\simeq B_n(P)[m]$ by the additive finite tensor shift followed by the additive restriction-of-scalars shift. Each has the identity degree component after reindexing. Define $\operatorname{completedScalarShiftProductIso}_{P,m}=\beta_{P,m}:X_{P[m]}\simeq X_P[m]$ as the product of these level maps followed by the inverse product-preservation comparison for shift. Thus its projection to every shifted factor is precisely the specified level map; its inverse is the product of the inverse degree reindexings. No tower or product isomorphism is chosen independently.

For a coherent integer shift structure $e_C$ on $C$, define $\operatorname{completedScalarShiftConeFormula}(e_C,P,m)$ by the following two equations. Write $u_P^j:X_P^j\to C(P)^j$ for the unshifted mapping-cocone inclusion and $v_P^{i,j}:X_P^i\to C(P)^j$ for the other inclusion, defined when $i+1=j$. These are the degree components of the two inclusions of the specified mapping cocone, not an assertion that both inclusions are chain maps. Let $r_{P,m,j}:C(P)[m]^j\simeq C(P)^{j+m}$ be standard degree reindexing. Require, for every $j\in\mathbf Z$ and every $i+1=j$,
$$\begin{aligned}
(e_{C,m,P})^j\circ u_{P[m]}^j
 &=r_{P,m,j}^{-1}\circ u_P^{j+m}\circ\beta_{P,m}^j,\\
(e_{C,m,P})^j\circ v_{P[m]}^{i,j}
 &=(-1)^m\,r_{P,m,j}^{-1}\circ v_P^{i+m,j+m}\circ\beta_{P,m}^i.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the prescribed map is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^m y)$ in mapping-cocone coordinates $C(P)^j=X_P^j\oplus X_P^{j-1}$, via the fixed product map and reindexing.

For $e_C$ and a coherent shift structure $e_T$ on $T$, define $\operatorname{completedScalarShiftIntegralNormalization}(e_C,e_T)$ to mean that for every good $P$ and integer $m$, there exists a witness that $P[m]$ is good and
$$d_P[m]\circ e_{T,m,QP}=\eta_{C(P),m}\circ Q(e_{C,m,P})\circ d_{P[m]}\circ T(\eta_{P,m}^{-1}).$$
Both sides are morphisms $T((QP)[m])\to(QC(P))[m]$. These are definitions of maps and predicates only: no existence of $e_C,e_T$, chain-shift compatibility, or descent theorem is asserted.
